newsitem.title: UK: Late origin/consumer selling hits palm in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Late origin/consumer selling hits palm in Europe.

text.p: A late burst of origin and consumer selling knocked off most of the gains in crude palm oil during Wednesday afternoon.
Plam oil prices had held steady for most of the day, supported by higher futures in Chicago and Asia, but traders said the market remained fundamental weak.
"One major refiner was doing most of the buying in Malaysia this morning and when he stopped the market dipped towards the close," said one trader.
Traders could not give a reason for the selling by origin and consumers at the lower levels.
"Someone must have found he can get replacement stocks at a lower price," said one.
Soft oils continued to draw support from higher Chicago futures on the back of talk of China business.
Earlier in the day traders in Shanghai said China had been buying significant quantities of U.S. soybeans and soymeal since early July as world prices slumped.
Among lauric oils coconut oil closed slightly higher in light trade while palmkernel oil was down on a neglected market.
At the close crude palm oil cif Europe was unchanged after Jul traded at $507.50 and Aug at $512.50 and $507.50 a tonne cif.
No further business was reported among palm products which finished with RBD oil $5 to $12.50 up and olein $2.50 up.

Dtuch soy oil closed 1.25 to 1.50 guilders higher in a tradeless market while rape oil was 0.75 to 1.25 guilders higher after Nov/Jan traded at 103.00 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill in outright business while Aug/Oct traded at 103.25 in a switch with Nov/Jan at even money.
Coconut oil sellers were $2.50 higher after Jul/Aug, Aug/Sep and Sep/Oct all traded at $602.50 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil finished $12.50 down to unchanged.
